Think your U P I money is invisible to the taxman? It isn't. Here's how to stay safe.
Rohan's chai stall takes U P I all day. Twenty rupees here, forty there.
His friend says, small U P I payments don't count. That's a myth.
There's no tax on U P I itself. But income is taxable, however you receive it. Cash, U P I, or bank.
And every U P I payment lands in your bank account. That's a permanent digital trail.
The tax department sees a lot through your Annual Information Statement, the A.I.S.. And it can ask for your bank records.
So, when does a notice come?
When the money in your bank is much higher than the income you declare.
Now meet a second Rohan. He follows three simple habits.
One. A separate account for the stall. Two. A note on every big credit. A friend repaying dinner isn't income.
Three. He checks his A.I.S. once a year, on the income tax portal, before he files.
AI can sort a year of bank entries in minutes. But for tax decisions, ask a C A.
U P I isn't the problem. Undeclared income is.
